findings.text: `final()` (Recite.js:~175) returns silently when `auto` is off or the reply is a duplicate, so a settled reply (the `chat.from.id === "smart"` and `replies.add` paths) leaves only "reply line" with no "not read: auto is off" line; only the streaming `partial()` path traces that skip. If the phone gets the reply as a line without a stream, the log cannot show why nothing was spoken, which is the owner's whole question.

Recite's readme (`audio/Recite/readme.md`) and the Whisper docs (`Whisper/readme.md` line 11, `doc/demo.md` line 28 "Other `src` values") do not mention the new `src:"recite"` lines or `trace()`. Per the "document the structure" law, add a line for what writes them, the kinds (unlocked by a tap, unlock refused, reply streaming, reply line, not read, spoke, speak failed, play refused, playing, paused by your line) and where to read them.

The task folder holds only requirements.md: no task.jsonl, notes or result line, so a fresh agent cannot tell what was verified (e.g. that `WhisperLog.event` lines from Recite appear at /framework/audio/Whisper/log/, and whether `WhisperLogRows` renders an unknown `src` sensibly).

The requirement lists "speak asked", but only the outcomes ("spoke", "speak failed") are traced, not the request itself; a speak that never returns (hung tunnel) leaves no line. A "speak asked" line at the start of `render()` (Recite.js:~127) would cover it.

`trace()` does a dynamic `import()` per line (cached by the browser after the first), and the `"reply streaming"` and `"not read"` lines are guarded by `!this.live`, so they do not spam per chunk; that is fine. No simpler route was found.
